title: Is a 0.1 drop in pH small?
hook: Ocean pH went from 8.2 to 8.1. Is that a 1% change?

knows: that pH is a log scale (ph-log-scale)
that lower pH means more acidic
doesNotKnow: that a fall of 0.1 in seawater pH is a rise of about 26% in hydrogen ion concentration

misconception: pH 8.2 to 8.1 is a trivial change of about 1%.
objective: The learner can explain that each 0.1 fall in pH multiplies the hydrogen ion concentration by 10^0.1, about 1.26, so the ocean's fall from about 8.2 to 8.1 is a rise of about 26%, and a fall of 0.3 is about a doubling.

claims.text: Surface seawater pH fell from about 8.2 to about 8.1 since pre-industrial times.
claims.source: IPCC SROCC (2019) ch. 1: surface pH down about 0.1 since the industrial era (high confidence), about 26% more acidity; NOAA PMEL 'Ocean acidification' (pre-industrial about 8.2, today about 8.1). Values are global means, rounded. · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Number holds (NOAA 8.21 to 8.10; IPCC SROCC ch.1: pH down 0.1 since industrial era, high confidence, 26% acidity). The cited AR6 "virtually certain" refers to the decline over ~40 years, not the 0.1 total; recommend citing SROCC ch.1 and NOAA instead.

claims.text: A fall of 0.1 in pH raises the hydrogen ion concentration by about 26% (10^0.1 = 1.26).
claims.source: pH = −log10[H+], so [H+] ratio = 10^(8.2 − 8.1) = 1.259 (node; Demo.tsx ratio()). The stage's 100 dots become 126.

claims.text: A fall of 0.3 in pH is about a doubling of hydrogen ions (10^0.3 = 2.0; the stage shows about 200 dots at pH 7.9 against 100 at pH 8.2).
claims.source: 10^0.3 = 1.995 (node); stage shows about 200 dots at pH 7.9. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): node: 10^0.3 = 1.995; Demo.tsx ratio(7.9) x 100 = 199.5, shown as about 200 against the 100 at pH 8.2. (Text reads "against 100 at pH 7.9"; the 100 is at pH 8.2: optional wording tidy, non-blocking.) | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 15): re-checked after wording fix. node: 10^(8.2-7.9) = 1.9953; Demo.tsx Math.round(100 x ratio(7.9)) = 200 dots, readout +100%, against REF_DOTS = 100 boxed at pH 8.2. Text now matches the stage.

claims.text: pH counts powers of ten of hydrogen ion concentration: one whole pH unit lower is ten times the hydrogen ions.
claims.source: pH = −log10 a(H+) (IUPAC Gold Book, 'pH'); concentration used in place of activity, as is usual at this level. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): IUPAC Gold Book pH = -lg a(H+); concentration-for-activity simplification stated in source.

claims.text: Lower pH means more hydrogen ions (H⁺).
claims.source: pH = -log10 of hydrogen ion concentration (standard definition); added by builder 2026-10-13 revision because the question now says it.

claims.text: Ten steps of 0.1 in pH make one whole unit, so each step multiplies the hydrogen ions by about 1.26, and 1.26 multiplied by itself ten times is about 10.

recall.question: A lake's pH falls from 7.0 to 6.7. Its hydrogen ion concentration has roughly…
recall.why: Each 0.1 down multiplies [H+] by about 1.26; 0.3 down is 10^0.3, about 2.
